## Goal

Make "won a game" a first-class, engine-generic achievement event so the give-away triggers have a real, Steam-free source.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AchievementSystem` (or a documented thin extension) gains an idempotent game-outcome surface (e.g. `onGameOutcome({ gameId, outcome })`) that unlocks mapped achievements via the existing `AchievementSink`; zero Steam/Electron imports.
- The launcher manifest defines `first-win` and `second-distinct-game-win` meta-achievements (titles, descriptions, hidden flags) and the outcome-to-achievement mapping is engine-generic.
- "Second distinct game" logic only unlocks after wins in two different game ids; re-wins of the same game do not.
- `SteamAchievementService` idempotence and offline paths are reused unchanged for the meta-achievements.
- Unit tests cover outcome-to-unlock, distinct-game counting, idempotence, and no-op for unknown outcomes; pass under `--project unit`.

## Key Files

- `src/core-engine/AchievementSystem.ts`
- `src/core-engine/index.ts`
- `electron/achievement-manifest.json`
- `tests/steam-achievements/achievement-outcome.test.ts` (new)

## Deliverables

Engine outcome surface, manifest meta-achievements, unit tests.
data.title: Engine game-outcome surface and cross-game meta-achievements

# Document The Rising ToneForge SFX in SFX_CONVENTION.md (full game audio profile)

## Goal

As an engine maintainer, I want The Rising's ToneForge-generated face-off SFX
documented as a first-class game audio profile in the shared
`docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md`, so sibling game repos have a complete, copyable
reference for the convention (keys, deterministic regeneration, runtime wiring,
fallback behaviour).

## Problem statement

`docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` documents the `sfx-` key convention, asset
organisation, playback helpers and collision protection, and it carries one
ToneForge precedent section (`## Main Street Synth SFX`). The Rising already
ships three ToneForge-generated face-off sounds, but the shared convention has
no The Rising entry — so the doc is incomplete for sibling repos and the
game-side knowledge lives only in `tce-the-rising/README.md`.

## Existing state

- `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` (in this repo) has no The Rising section, and the
  `## Audio Asset Organization` tree lists `default/`, `golf/`, `sushi-go/`,
  `feudalism/`, `beleaguered-castle/`, `lost-cities/`, `main-street/` — no
  `the-rising/`.
- The Rising keeps its audio in its **own** repo
  (`tce-the-rising/public/assets/audio/the-rising/`), loaded through the
  pinned `core` submodule; no assets are vendored into the engine.
- The game README (§ *Regenerating the face-off SFX*) already records the
  authoritative facts:
  - `sfx-face-off-reveal` → `face-off-reveal.wav` —
    `tf generate --recipe card-treasure-reveal --seed 42`
  - `sfx-float-in-whoosh` → `float-in-whoosh.wav` —
    `tf generate --recipe whoosh-air-swish --seed 43`
  - `sfx-land-tick` → `land-tick.wav` —
    `tf generate --recipe card-timer-tick --seed 44`
  - keys in `THERISING_SFX_KEYS` (`src/scenes/TheRisingConstants.ts`), file
    mappings in `THERISING_AUDIO_FILES`, preloaded via `preload()` +
    `audioPathWithFallback`, played only via `SoundManager`/`safePlaySound`.
- The game plays all three beats when reduced motion is enabled (no travel, but
  audio still fires).
- The Rising has **no** ToneForge synth mapping module (unlike Main Street's
  `example-games/main-street/sfx-tf-mapping.ts`) — playback falls through to
  committed WAV assets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` gains a `## The Rising ToneForge SFX` section
  documenting the three keys, their asset filenames under
  `public/assets/audio/the-rising/`, and the exact deterministic
  `tf generate --recipe <recipe> --seed <int> --output <path>` command for each
  (seeds 42 / 43 / 44 as recorded in the game README).
- AC2 — The `## Audio Asset Organization` tree gains a `the-rising/` entry
  noting the assets live in the game repo
  (`tce-the-rising/public/assets/audio/the-rising/`), mirroring the existing
  Main Street parenthetical.
- AC3 — The profile records runtime wiring: keys declared in
  `THERISING_SFX_KEYS` (`src/scenes/TheRisingConstants.ts`), file mappings in
  `THERISING_AUDIO_FILES`, loading through `preload()` +
  `audioPathWithFallback()`, playback only through
  `SoundManager`/`safePlaySound` (`no-direct-sound-play` rule).
- AC4 — The profile records reduced-motion behaviour: with reduced motion
  enabled the face-off animation is instant but all three SFX beats still play.
- AC5 — The profile states fallback behaviour: the three face-off WAVs are
  game-specific with no `default/` equivalent, the nine baseline SFX fall back
  to `default/`, and there is no ToneForge synth mapping for The Rising (so
  playback resolves to WAV assets).
- AC6 — The profile links the game-side reproducibility instructions
  (`tce-the-rising/README.md` § *Regenerating the face-off SFX*) and states the
  section is maintained in the engine because sibling game repos read this doc.
- AC7 — Documentation-only change: no engine code, constants or behaviour is
  altered, and `npm run build` + `npm test` pass on the docs branch.
- AC8 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC9 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Docs-only: no engine code behaviour change; no new engine SFX keys.
- Do not copy The Rising's WAV assets into the engine repo (assets stay in the
  game repo, referenced by path).
- Only `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` is expected to change; `CHANGELOG.md` is managed
  by the release pipeline.
- Landed on engine `dev` through the normal flow. Producer decision
  (2026-10-19): the consuming game repo (`tce-the-rising`) pins its `core`
  submodule to the **`dev` commit containing this change**, rather than waiting
  for the `dev` → `main` release promotion — so the commit SHA must be reported
  on completion for the cross-repo pointer bump.

## Key Files

- `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` — new `## The Rising ToneForge SFX` section; add
  `the-rising/` to the `## Audio Asset Organization` tree.

## Related work

- Cross-repo tracker: **RISE-0MVBUSQUR006LPVP** (tce-the-rising) — blocked by
  this item; on completion it bumps its `core` submodule pointer to this item's
  engine `dev` commit and verifies the doc renders in-tree. Report the commit
  SHA in the completion comment so the game-side bump is deterministic.
- `RISE-0MVBKG7VK003JIDH` (tce-the-rising) — generated the three WAVs and
  recorded the recipes/seeds this section documents.
- Precedent: `## Main Street Synth SFX` in the same doc, and
  `example-games/main-street/sfx-tf-mapping.ts` for the synth-mapping contrast.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (drift):** recipes/seeds recorded in the game README could diverge from
  this section. Mitigation: quote the exact commands and link the README section
  as the authority.
- **Risk (inverted dependency):** documenting another repo's assets in the
  engine could imply the engine owns them. Mitigation: state explicitly that
  assets live in the game repo and the engine only owns the convention text.
- **Assumption:** the three recipe names/seeds in the game README are the
  committed, reproducible values (verified there; recorded in
  RISE-0MVBKG7VK003JIDH as byte-identical on regeneration).
- **Assumption:** a docs-only engine change still needs the normal
  build+test gate, per engine policy.
data.title: Document The Rising ToneForge SFX in SFX_CONVENTION.md (full game audio profile)

# Restore engine dev build/test green: unused imports + stale card-pack CSV header

## Problem statement

`origin/dev` tip (e4d0e10b) is red for two pre-existing reasons, both unrelated
to consumer work but both blocking any push to `dev` (the pre-push hook runs the
full suite):

1. **Build break.** `tsc --noEmit` fails with two TS6133 errors in
   `tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` (introduced by a1de8717,
   CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q):
   - line 24: 'fileURLToPath' is declared but its value is never read.
   - line 146: 'f' is declared but its value is never read.
2. **Test failure.** `tests/scripts/build-card-pack.test.ts` asserts the
   reference Main Street pack CSV header equals the *generic* 53-column
   `CARD_PACK_CSV_HEADER` from `tests/fixtures/card-pack/helpers.ts`, but the
   committed reference fixture was intentionally re-synced to the 55-column
   production schema (a1560d4d / dc4ec0ce: added `options` and
   `piggybackable`). The reference test was never updated, so it compares a
   55-column copy against a 53-column constant. (Bumping the shared constant
   is wrong: the merge/UI fixtures under `tests/fixtures/card-pack/packs/` are
   deliberately 53-column and use it as their base schema.)

Both defects block CG-0MVFQ6QOZ003FVO4 (docs-only SFX_CONVENTION.md change),
whose AC7/AC9 require build + full suite to pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — `tsc --noEmit` passes: remove the unused `fileURLToPath` import and the
  unused `const f = makeFixture();` in the 'is true when the submodule is not
  (yet) a git repo' test.
- AC2 — The reference-pack assertion compares the copied header against the
  committed reference fixture's own header (55-column schema), not the generic
  `CARD_PACK_CSV_HEADER`; the merge/UI fixtures and their 53-column base-schema
  constant are left unchanged.
- AC3 — `npm run build` passes.
- AC4 — `npm test` passes.

## Constraints

- Test-support only; no production code altered.
- UK English.
- Blocks CG-0MVFQ6QOZ003FVO4 (recorded textually).

## Key Files

- `tests/scripts/engine-sync.test.ts` — remove unused import/variable.
- `tests/scripts/build-card-pack.test.ts` — reference-pack header assertion
  (derive expected header from the committed fixture).
data.title: Restore engine dev build/test green: unused imports + stale card-pack CSV header
